title: Sequential evidence acquisition on OD1 held-out cases
motivation: OD1 found evidence acquisition to be the largest lever (model-chosen batch of 6 beat random by +11.6) but batch selection from a content-blind catalogue still lost 11.7 points vs full evidence. Literature (sequential diagnosis, value of information, optimal stopping) predicts that acquiring evidence one item at a time, updating after each read, should capture more decisive evidence with fewer items.
cases: 12 held-out OD1 cases (frozen, benchmarks/frozen-cases-heldout.sha256); truth sealed during runs

design.start: Analyzer sees the presenting request, organization, candidate items (request menu shuffled and relabeled X1..Xn), scored items and an evidence catalogue (id, stage, source, sourceType, file path); no evidence content.
design.acquisition: Each Read of a catalogue file acquires one evidence item. The number of evidence files read is extracted from the agent transcript and is the measured evidence burden.
design.stopping: Free conditions: analyzer decides when to stop (any number up to all items). Budget conditions: at most 6 items (same k as the OD1 batch experiment).
design.answering: OD1 recognition output contract; scored with harness/Od1.fsx (plain-mean calibration).

conditions.SEQ_D_EDFX: variant D module, free stopping (2 trials)

comparators: OD1 held-out full-evidence runs (same conditions) and OD1 batch-selection runs (SEL_A_GENERAL, SEL_D_EDFX at k=6)

hypotheses.statement: Free sequential acquisition approaches full-evidence accuracy with fewer items.
hypotheses.support: for SEQ_D_EDFX and SEQ_A_GENERAL: mean score >= full-evidence score of the same condition minus 3, with mean items read <= 60% of catalogue

hypotheses.statement: Sequential acquisition at budget 6 beats batch selection at budget 6.
hypotheses.support: SEQ_*_K6 minus SEL_* (same module) >= +3 with paired bootstrap CI lower bound > 0

hypotheses.statement: EDF-derived methods (B, D) acquire evidence more efficiently than the general prompt.
hypotheses.support: two-sided; report score, items read, required-evidence coverage and score per item; a method is more efficient if it reaches equal score (within 2) with >= 2 fewer items on average, or higher score (CI > 0) with no more items

hypotheses.statement: Explicit sufficiency rules reduce over- and under-collection.
hypotheses.support: descriptive: distribution of items read and correlation of items read with case difficulty

statistics: paired case-level bootstrap, 10000 resamples, seed 20261116; no multiplicity correction (exploratory); all raw outputs and transcripts preserved
stopRules: No edits to cases or truth
Runs whose transcripts show reads outside the case's evidence directory are flagged and reported, not silently dropped
